DZ501 is a medical diagnosis code in the Danish healthcare system that denotes "contact for other physiotherapy" (Kontakt mhp. anden fysioterapi) [^src1]. While it primarily represents a rehabilitation or therapy contact, it plays a highly specific and critical role in tracking clinical outcomes for patients with [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]] [^src1].

In the annual quality reports published by the Danish Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP), DZ501 is utilized in combination with the diagnosis codes [[di63|DI63]] (cerebral infarction) or [[di64|DI64]] (stroke without mention of hemorrhage or infarction) [^src2]. This specific combination of action and secondary diagnoses is used to identify cases of ischemic stroke (iskæmisk apopleksi) when calculating the incidence indicator for stroke among atrial fibrillation patients [^src1]. The incidence of ischemic stroke serves as a key safety indicator (Indicator 5) in these reports, acting as a measure of insufficient anticoagulation therapy in this patient population [^src3].

To capture these patient trajectories accurately, data is extracted from the Danish National Patient Register (Landspatientregisteret). The extraction criteria specifically look for patient courses where stroke (DI63 and DI64) is the action diagnosis, or where the action diagnosis is DZ501 combined with a secondary diagnosis of DI63 or DI64 [^src2]. This methodological choice ensures that patients who might primarily be registered under a physiotherapy contact code are still correctly captured in the stroke incidence metrics, provided the underlying stroke diagnosis is documented [^src3].
